My Aggressive Daily-Routine as an Open-Source Advocate When I grew up as a child, I always wondered how these people managed to fucking run these fancy neovim setups and all these flashing windows moving around on their screen. I had this desire to find out what they were doing, ever since I was in the womb. Once I realised how much data every company is harvesting from you—I pivoted, and never came back—it's been the most wonderful journey I have experienced.
Ever since I was a child, I've been starting to love using Neovim more. I've realised how the corporate monopolies (Microsoft, Visual Studio Code) have actually been trying to HINDER our abilities to create things! YouTube—from Google has also been doing this, same with TikTok and all that typeof() stuff. Crazy, isn't it?? Here's a quote from when I was a child:
When I use Neovim—I will fucking surpass humanity, soar to the skies, climb to the top of the corporate ladder (i will even break the corporate ladder) to make more profit all because I have learned how to surpass humanity with the ultimate skill of editing text, blazingly fast. I will shift mountains, shift seas, and shift humanity towards a better future by editing their genome sequences and making everything software-based so it's more reliable than ever.
Crazy visions, crazy visions. Am I right? Wow. How insightful. This goal is ultimately too difficult to achieve though, and I don't think climbing the corporate ladder nor making profit is very useful. Infact, what happened with corporations? What? WHAT???
"Oh yes I love making money and oh yeah I'm just a corporation I need more money and uhhh... Yeah one time we killed a few people because.. Maybe not one time though.. Probably many times... We're humans right?? Humans make mistakes??? I mean... Or we might have killed more than a few people actually... But look at the human population! 8 billion people. These delicious metrics. I don't think we are a cause of danger, right? We're actually truly dedicated to safety—we would never harm anyone! We are so safe, and we care about our mission. Everyone loves our products! We just added another AI feature, it's quite lively we'd say—our stocks increased by 2% this quarter, which is a big sign that everyone is enjoying it. Look at our metrics! 95% shareholder happiness! Wow. Truly amazing." - yours, corporation. Anyways, back to my actual daily routine. In the mornings, I wake up from my LibreBed and they come with an pre-built blanket which is very cool. Normally, these beds are wayy too closed source. Infact, last week I just bought one of these amazing beds that feel sooo comfyyyy and the blankets they came with are sooo cozy and memory-safe! I configured it to my liking, better than a corporate bed could ever be—I can never go back now. After that, I brush my teeth with NeoBrush while I watch the lights flicker with my Anubis-Light as it catches those evil scrapers—this light protects you from the horrors of AI scrapers looking into your bathroom. They truly can be scary. Now for my work? I don't work. I don't like closed-source stuff. All this corporate nonsense, actually. I have made the work and open-sourced it! I am open-sourcing my new currency if you want to see. I have somehow survived starvation because I open sourced my body and removed the starvation feature that all these people on the world are trying to trick you on human history being a thing and food being required to live. That's just straight BS! Just open-source your body, and you can config it as much as you want—away from those hindering flaws they deliberately injected into you. Become one with the machine—it has worked for me. When everything is open-source, I can just accept a pull request that someone makes, and instantly get changes for everyone. That annoying bug that was flying in your house? No need to wait for the closed-source bug to be met with your closed-source house. Just simply, fix the bug in the source code. It's so easy, no need to wait for a corporate solution like these pesky fly rackets they ask you to pay for.
It's actually a quite peaceful time in humanity, I'd say—so, I would go to the AptShop to check on what new, cutting-edge, blazingly fast grocery repositories have been released. Turns out, not many. But the existing ones are improving! So I simply just update my existing ones and make some delicious Hash Maps with BeEF in some Java coffee (don't use the oracle one) for dinner. After that, I enjoy a couple of rounds of taking pictures at the moon with a LibreCamera that I have specifically configured it to ponder on life's questions while formatting it into a png.
And there's my day! I hope you enjoyed reading this and consuming words, until next time.
